name: DFER-CLIP
authors_or_creators: Zengqun Zhao and Ioannis Patras, Queen Mary University of London (QMUL)
backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 (image encoder) with Transformer-based temporal module; CLIP text encoder
accuracy_affectnet: not reported (DFER-CLIP targets dynamic FER benchmarks, not AffectNet) [uncertain]
accuracy_rafdb: not reported (DFER-CLIP targets dynamic FER benchmarks, not RAF-DB)
pretrained_weights_available: yes - released via the official GitHub repository (CLIP-ViT-B/32 based checkpoints for DFEW, FERV39k, MAFW)
hardware_requirements: Training reported on NVIDIA GPUs (single/multi-GPU); CLIP ViT-B/32 backbone makes it tractable on a single high-end GPU (e.g., RTX 3090/A100). Exact configuration not strongly specified [uncertain]
loss_function: Cross-entropy classification loss combined with CLIP-style image-text contrastive alignment between the temporal visual feature and learnable class-name text prompts
training_data_used: DFEW, FERV39k, MAFW (each benchmark trained on its own training split using its standard protocol, e.g., 5-fold cross-validation on DFEW)
pretraining_strategy: VLM-pretrain (initialized from CLIP pretrained weights); fine-tuned on dynamic FER datasets
pretraining_corpus: OpenAI CLIP WIT (400M image-text pairs) used for CLIP pretraining; downstream FER training on DFEW/FERV39k/MAFW
input_modality: video clip (RGB frames) with text-conditioned class descriptors (learnable text prompts)
dynamic_fer_metrics: DFEW: ~71.25% WAR / ~59.61% UAR; FERV39k: ~52.55% WAR / ~41.27% UAR; MAFW: ~52.55% WAR / ~39.89% UAR (5-fold protocol; values as reported in the BMVC 2023 paper) [uncertain]
cross_dataset_generalization: not systematically reported in the paper [uncertain]
robustness: not specifically evaluated on Occlusion-RAF-DB / Pose-RAF-DB benchmarks [uncertain]
explainability: Attention maps from the temporal Transformer can be visualized; learnable text prompts provide class-level semantic interpretability
